analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1116-1128, in the unit starting at base line 1116). It describes the Qwen inline MTP assistant's ordinary-decode history chaining for multi-row decode, a prefill carry from the final prompt row's hidden state, an opt-in via `supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory`, and two rollback env switches (`DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED` and `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY`). No executable code is in the supplied evidence, so the actual source behavior (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift) was not reviewed. Security relevance is limited. The hidden-state history is in-process engine state, which is the same plaintext-in-memory exposure already covered by TB-007 and T-028/T-011/T-014. The doc says there is no extra readback and no persistence of in-flight speculative state. It does not touch the SSD prefix-cache surface (T-041): the TTL, HMAC lookup tags, salts and gating are unchanged. I found no new trust boundary, no changed secret handling, and no encryption or authorization regression. Remaining questions for later passes, which cannot be answered from this docs-only diff: (1) whether the carry or history is cleared or isolated correctly per request, so no cross-request hidden-state leakage occurs (T-028); (2) whether the carry or history is wired into the prefix-checkpoint path, since those states must not be serialized outside the existing authenticated DBK3 contract. Neither is a finding without source evidence.
